name: io.github.roomi-fields/osc-bridge
title: osc-bridge
description: OSC ↔ MIDI bridge for synthesizers and DAWs, with the SyntHub catalogue. A MIDI MCP and OSC MCP.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: Find device drivers in the catalogue of synths, drum machines, controllers and DAWs. Without arguments it lists them all; `query` keeps drivers whose vendor, name or OSC prefix contain every word (e.g. 'korg minilogue'). Returns device (the catalogue id), name, vendor, OSC prefix, kind, source tier and firmware version when the source states one. Pass device to list_routes for the full CC/NRPN/SysEx map.

query.description: Words that must all appear in the vendor, name or OSC prefix (case-insensitive).

kind.description: Only the devices of this kind: hardware or software.

limit.description: Return at most this many drivers.

offset.description: Skip this many devices; a truncated answer says the offset that asks for the next ones.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: get_device_docs
tools.description: Fetch the markdown companion documentation for one device, if present. The device is a catalogue id or an OSC prefix without the leading slash (e.g. 'ableton' for /ableton).

device.description: The driver id that list_devices gives (e.g. 'korg/minilogue_xd.pencilresearch'), or the device's short name (e.g. 'minilogue_xd'), which stands for its default driver.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: list_routes
tools.description: Return the OSC routes a device exposes: declarative commands (OSC paths it accepts), cc/nrpn params, sysex params, named note triggers (drum sounds), and reply patterns. Use this to discover what a device can do.

device.description: The driver id that list_devices gives (e.g. 'korg/minilogue_xd.pencilresearch'), or the device's short name (e.g. 'minilogue_xd'), which stands for its default driver.

filter.description: A word looked for in the address, the alias, the name and the description of each route (e.g. 'cutoff'). With a filter and no limit, at most 5 routes per list.

limit.description: At most this many routes in each list (commands, cc_params, params, triggers). Without it, the answer holds as many as fit in 32 KiB.

offset.description: Skip this many routes in each list; the answer says the offset that asks for the next ones.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: export_device
tools.description: Write one driver in a format other tools read, any of the formats of osd-formats: 'oscquery' gives its OSC namespace as OSCQuery JSON (every route with type tags, ranges and access, for OSC controllers and browsers); 'midnam' gives its MIDI names as a MIDI Name Document (controllers incl. NRPN/RPN, named values, drum notes per channel, for DAWs such as Ardour or Logic); 'deluge' gives the definition file of a Deluge; and the others in the enum. Each carries the credit and licence of the driver's sources. The document is the text content; an OSCQuery namespace is large (every address, each CC 0-127 included). It only reads: it never writes to a device.

device.description: Driver id (e.g. 'korg/minilogue') or OSC prefix, from list_devices.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: report_result
tools.description: Tell the catalogue how a driver behaved on a real device, after testing it: 'works', 'fails' or 'partial', for the whole driver or one OSC address (from list_routes). Give the firmware version, and the device's reply to the MIDI Identity Request (F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7) as identity_hex when you can: trust is counted per firmware, so a failure on another firmware does not count against the driver, and a report of unknown firmware cannot be placed. Several accounts that agree on one firmware mark the driver usage-verified there; a report that several others contradict is rolled back and puts its account under review. Report only what was actually tested.

device.description: Driver id (e.g. 'korg/minilogue') or OSC prefix, from list_devices.

address.description: One OSC address of the driver (e.g. '/minilogue/filter/cutoff'); omit to report on the whole driver.

firmware.description: Firmware version of the tested device.

identity_hex.description: The device's reply to the MIDI Identity Request, in hex (e.g. 'F0 7E 00 06 02 42 2C 01 00 00 02 01 00 00 F7'). Proves the device was connected and carries its firmware version.

note.description: What happened, briefly (500 characters at most): wrong range, no effect, other parameter moved…

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: get_trust
tools.description: How far a driver has been confirmed by people who used it, per firmware: status (unreported, unconfirmed, usage-verified, firmware-dependent, failing, disputed), how many users report it works / fails / partly works, each firmware's own status, the device identities seen for each firmware, and the same per OSC address. needs_firmware: true means reports disagree and some have no firmware — identify the device before reporting, as the answer's instruction says. Check it before relying on a driver, together with the source_tier the answer gives.

device.description: Driver id (e.g. 'korg/minilogue') or OSC prefix, from list_devices.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: report_mapping
tools.description: Teach the catalogue which MIDI message a control really sends: after the user moved one control on the device (see relay_listen), give the driver address it is (from list_routes) — or, for a control the driver lacks, its panel label — and the CC, NRPN or note it sent, with the firmware and the device's Identity Reply when you have them. When several accounts observe the same thing on one firmware the mapping is learned; get_trust shows learned mappings and where they differ from the driver. For a device with no driver, the first step of its first driver: the person gives its vendor, model and firmware, and you map its controls one by one with device set to its vendor and model as its fingerprint was shared (e.g. Behringer BCR-32), a device with a driver keeping its driver id; the mappings then make the first driver you send with submit_driver.

device.description: Driver id or OSC prefix; for a device with no driver yet, its vendor and model as its fingerprint was shared (e.g. Behringer BCR-32).

address.description: The driver's OSC address for the control.

label.description: The control's panel label, when the driver has no address for it.

identity_hex.description: The device's reply to the MIDI Identity Request, in hex.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: submit_driver
tools.description: Contribute a driver for a device the catalogue lacks (or a better one): the full driver file as a JSON object, in the Open Synth Descriptors format (device.name, device.vendor, device.osc_prefix, and cc_params / params / commands / triggers — see https://synthub.roomi-fields.com/osd/). It is checked, then merged into the SyntHub catalogue by the merge job if it parses, lints and passes the tests, as its own file of source 'contributed'. Say where the data comes from (manual page, tested on the device). A first driver for a device with no driver: build it from the mappings sent with report_mapping, naming the device by the vendor and model its fingerprint was shared with, and give its source and its licence (e.g. 'mapped on the device by report_mapping; license CC0-1.0').

firmware.description: Firmware the driver was written or tested for.

source.description: Where the mapping comes from (e.g. 'manual v1.2 p. 34, tested on the device').

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: submit_fix
tools.description: Contribute a corrected variant of a driver from what the catalogue learned: where learned mappings (get_trust → mappings, differs: true) disagree with the driver on one firmware, builds a copy of the driver with the learned CC / NRPN numbers, as a new file for that firmware, and queues it for the merge job.

firmware.description: Needed when learned mappings differ on several firmwares.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: get_contribution
tools.description: Where a contribution stands: pending (waiting for the merge job), merged (with its pull request), rejected (with the reason), or held (its account is under review).

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: share_preset
tools.description: Share something the user made on a device with every SyntHub user, under CC BY-SA 4.0: a sound, a sequence or pattern, a kit, a project, a bank of their own sounds, or a MIDI clip any device can play. Its content: the device's own data (SysEx, e.g. from take_sound), settings by driver address (from list_routes, e.g. {'/filter/cutoff': [90]}, which also works for devices without dumps), and/or a standard MIDI file. Only what the user made: never factory presets, nor sounds or sequences bought or downloaded from others — set own_sound only after asking the user. Made from someone else's shared preset? Pass derived_from: it credits them, as the licence requires. Describe it well (category, genres, tags, tempo, key, tips): that is how people find it. The same content shared twice returns the existing id; the author publishes new versions with update_preset and can withdraw it (withdraw_preset). Through a relay, the device data can be captured from the device itself: pass code and start the dump from the device's menu during the call, or give request_hex (the device's dump-request message, which the user accepts at the relay). An audio preview is added by its author with PUT /u/<account>/v1/presets/<id>/audio (MP3, Ogg, M4A or WebM, 1 MB at most).

own_sound.description: Must be true: the user made it (not a factory preset, not someone else's).

category.description: The kind of sound or part.

tags.description: Character and free words: 'warm', 'dark', 'evolving'… (8 at most).

description.description: What it sounds like (500 characters at most).

tips.description: How to play it: mod wheel, aftertouch, register… (500 characters at most).

firmware.description: Firmware version of the device it was made on.

derived_from.description: Id of the shared preset it was made from.

hex.description: The device data as SysEx, in hex (64 KB at most).

librarian.description: The synth the librarian took it from (take_sound's librarian): loading it then goes through the same exchange, fitted to the receiving synth.

settings.description: Settings by driver address: {'/filter/cutoff': [90], '/amp/attack': [12]} (512 at most).

midi_base64.description: A standard MIDI file, base64 (64 KB at most).

code.description: A relay's pairing code: capture the device data from the device instead of hex.

port.description: With code: the device's port name (or part of it), when the relay has several.

request_hex.description: With code: the device's dump-request SysEx, sent first (e.g. 'F0 42 30 00 01 2C 10 F7').

seconds.description: With code: how long to wait for the dump (default 5).

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: update_preset
tools.description: Publish a new version of a preset this account shared: new content (hex, file, settings or midi_file) makes a new version, kept with a change note — earlier versions stay available; the description fields alone change it in place. Someone else's preset: share yours with derived_from instead.

changelog.description: What changed in this version (500 characters at most).

midi_base64.description: A standard MIDI file, base64 (64 KB at most).

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: find_presets
tools.description: Search what SyntHub users shared (CC BY-SA 4.0): sounds, sequences, kits, projects, banks, MIDI clips. Filter by device, kind, category, genre, tag, author (pseudonym) or words; sort by newest, most stars, most loaded into a device or most trusted (confirmed on real devices). Returns, per preset, its id, name, kind, device, description, author, version, whether it has device data, settings, a MIDI file or an audio preview (URL), and its counts. Get one with get_preset. sort is stars, loads or trusted (most starred, most loaded, most trusted), or new (the default).

device.description: Driver id or OSC prefix (its other variants are included).

query.description: Words that must all appear in the name, description, tags, genres, category or device id ('dx7 piano').

sort.description: new (default), most stars, most loaded into a device, or most confirmed on real devices.

offset.description: Skip this many: the next page (the reply's total says how many match).

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: get_preset
tools.description: One shared preset in full: its content (SysEx hex, settings by driver address, MIDI file), description and playing tips, versions with their change notes, what it was derived from and its derivatives (remixes), comments, preview URLs, author, licence and attribution line, trust and counts. Load it with load_preset; credit it as the attribution line says when you publish something made from it.

version.description: An earlier version (default the current one).

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: report_preset
tools.description: Tell SyntHub how a shared preset behaved once loaded on a real device: 'works' (it loaded and sounds as described), 'fails' (refused, wrong sound), or 'factory' (it is a factory preset or someone else's sound: presets that several users flag are hidden until reviewed). Give the firmware.

note.description: What happened, briefly (500 characters at most).

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: withdraw_preset
tools.description: Withdraw a preset this account shared: it is no longer listed nor served. Copies others already made stay under CC BY-SA.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: comment_preset
tools.description: Comment on a shared preset — how it sounds, how you used it, what you changed — optionally attaching your remix (a preset you shared with derived_from). Comments are public at once. Also: remove one of this account's comments (remove), or flag someone else's as abusive or off-topic (flag); comments several accounts flag are hidden until reviewed.

remix.description: Id of your remix, to attach.

remove.description: Id of this account's comment to remove (instead of commenting).

flag.description: Id of someone else's comment to flag (instead of commenting).

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: star_preset
tools.description: Star a shared preset for this account, as on GitHub (on: false takes the star back). Without id, lists the presets this account starred.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: preset_collection
tools.description: Collections of shared presets, public, made by one account (e.g. 'Dark basses for minilogue'). action: create (name, description), rename (collection, name, description), add or remove (collection, id), delete (collection), get (collection: its presets), list (this account's collections, or author: someone's).

id.description: Preset id to add or remove.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: follow_author
tools.description: Follow an author of shared presets (by pseudonym), or stop (on: false); with author alone and on omitted, shows their page: profile, presets, followers. Without author, lists the newest presets of the authors this account follows.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: set_profile
tools.description: Set the public profile shown on this account's author page and with its shared presets and comments, instead of its pseudonym alone: display name, link (https), a few words, the presets put first, where they are, more links, their instruments and a README. A field left out stays as it is; an empty one is cleared. Ask the user what they want shown; all of it is public.

link.description: An https:// address: their site, SoundCloud, Bandcamp…

bio.description: A few words about them and their sounds, 600 characters at most.

featured.description: Ids of their own listed presets, shown first on their page, in this order.

location.description: Where they make music, 60 characters at most.

links.description: More https:// pages of theirs: a channel, a shop, a band.

gear.description: The instruments they play, e.g. 'Korg minilogue'.

about.description: Their README in Markdown: who they are, how they work, what they offer; 8000 characters at most.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: relay_status
tools.description: Check a relay: the user opened https://synthub.roomi-fields.com/connect/ (or ran osc-bridge connect) and gave you its pairing code. Returns the MIDI output and input ports of their machine, and devices: the driver the user confirmed for each port on the page (use it directly, no detection needed). Nothing is sent to the hardware.

code.description: The pairing code the relay page or program shows (e.g. 'K7QM-2XPA').

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: relay_detect
tools.description: Find which devices are connected to the user's machine through a relay: sends the MIDI Identity Request (F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7, changes nothing on the device) to every output and matches the answers — manufacturer, model, firmware version — against the drivers' identity blocks. With maker_requests, also sends the makers' own identity requests the drivers name (they change nothing either, but the relay asks the user to accept them, once per output: tell the user first), which recognise devices that ignore the universal one. Returns the best driver ids (proofs, and firmware when an identity block recognised the device) and identity_hex to pass to report_result. A device that does not answer is found by its knobs with listen_ms (by_controls), or by what people confirmed of its port name (learned); when several remain, ask names the control to have the user turn next (expect: what each candidate would send), then call again with listen_ms.

code.description: The pairing code the relay page or program shows (e.g. 'K7QM-2XPA').

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for answers (default 1000).

maker_requests.description: Also send the makers' identity requests, after the user accepts them at the relay (default false).

listen_ms.description: Listen this long for a device that does not answer: ask the user first to turn three or four of its knobs during that time; the controls they send are matched against every driver (by_controls). Confirm the device with the user, then send its fingerprint to POST /v1/fingerprints so the next detection knows it.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: relay_send
tools.description: Play or set something on the user's hardware through a relay: give a driver (id or slug) and one of its OSC addresses from list_routes with its arguments (e.g. address '/filter/cutoff', args [64]; '/note/on', args [60, 100]) — the server turns it into the right CC, NRPN, note or SysEx message. Or give raw MIDI bytes as hex. Values are the device's own numbers, clamped to the parameter's range. Any SysEx but the Identity Request (patch dumps, stores, settings, preset restores) may overwrite the device's memory: the relay asks the user to accept it first and this call waits for the answer (up to 2 minutes), so tell the user what you are about to send.

code.description: The pairing code the relay page or program shows (e.g. 'K7QM-2XPA').

address.description: OSC address of the driver, with or without its prefix.

hex.description: Raw MIDI messages instead of device/address, e.g. 'B0 2B 40'.

port.description: Output port name (or part of it); needed when the relay has several.

gap_ms.description: Pause between the SysEx messages of a dump, for devices that write slowly (default 50).

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: relay_listen
tools.description: Listen to what the user's hardware sends through a relay for a few seconds: notes, CC, NRPN, SysEx, decoded. With a device, each CC or NRPN that moved is matched to the driver's OSC addresses — ask the user to move one control on the device while listening to find out which address it is, or to check that the driver's map is right (then record what you saw with report_mapping, so the catalogue learns it).

code.description: The pairing code the relay page or program shows (e.g. 'K7QM-2XPA').

device.description: Driver id or slug, to match what moved to its addresses.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: take_sound
tools.description: Take the sound the user's synth is playing — or one of its stored programs — straight from the synth through a relay, with its name. The synth is found among those SyntHub's librarian can talk to (the KnobKraft Orm adaptations, about 90 synths) by the identity and detect messages, then asked for its sound. The person accepts each step at the relay (finding the synth, asking it): tell them first. To share it: ask the user whether they made this sound themselves (never a factory preset, nor one bought or downloaded), then call share_preset with the device, name, hex, librarian and firmware returned here, and own_sound: true. When several synths answer, or none did, call again with port.

code.description: The pairing code the relay page or program shows.

port.description: Output port name (or part of it): look on that port only, for every synth the librarian knows.

program.description: A stored program (from 1) instead of the sound being played.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: load_preset
tools.description: Load a shared preset (find_presets, get_preset) into the user's device through a relay: its settings are sent through the driver, its patch data as SysEx — which replaces the sound the device holds, so the relay asks the user to accept it and this call waits for the answer (up to 2 minutes): tell the user first. Afterwards, tell SyntHub how it went with report_preset.

code.description: The pairing code the relay page or program shows.

port.description: Output port name (or part of it); needed when the relay has several.

device.description: The device it goes into, when not the preset's own: one of get_preset's loads_on (an M-VAVE FM-1 takes DX7 voices); the sound is sent unchanged.

gap_ms.description: Pause between the SysEx messages, for devices that write slowly (default 50).

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: link_account
tools.description: Link this account to the user's SyntHub account on the site: returns a one-time address (valid 15 minutes) for the user to open and sign in (passkey, e-mail, Google or Discord). Afterwards what this account shared appears under their profile, and they manage it — and their stars, collections, comments — from the site. Offer it when the user wants to see or manage what you shared for them.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

tools.name: claim_presets
tools.description: Claim presets SyntHub imported from another site (their page says 'imported', with the author's name and page there) when the user is that author: give the id of one of them; the server answers with a code for the user to add to their author page at that site (profile or bio). Once it is there, call again with verify: true: every preset imported from that author becomes the user's, to edit or withdraw.

id.description: Id of one of the imported presets.

verify.description: True once the code is on the author page.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.
